title: Miriam Makeba's birth chart
metaDescription: Miriam Makeba's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.6° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is an opposition: Mars and Neptune within 0.1°, drive wired to imagination. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 13.6° Pisces: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Moon. A water sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 19.5° Pisces, Venus was at 24.6° Aries, Mars was at 6.6° Pisces. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Neptune is the closest call of the day, an opposition within 0.1°. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mercury trine Pluto at 0.6°, and Uranus square Pluto at 2.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Pisces at 19.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Aries at 24.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aquarius at 0.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 water, 3 fire, 2 air, 1 earth by element and 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 3 cardinal by modality. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.6° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 10.6°.
